review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the candidates against the Hölder/`MemLp.smul` API in LpSeminorm/CompareExp.lean and the later `smul_of_top_*` lemmas. Most other repeated shapes are thin wrappers (`rw [← memLp_one_iff_integrable]; exact …`), short calculations, or one-line corollaries, which the rubric excludes. Two candidates are reported. None of the rewrites has been compiled. The `essSup` rewrite depends on an `eLpNorm_exponent_top`-style conversion and on a reorder or relaxed typeclass for `smul_of_top_left`. The `withDensity` finding is only a modest duplication.

findings.excerpt: have hg' : eLpNorm g ∞ μ ≠ ∞ := by rwa [eLpNorm_exponent_top g_aestronglyMeasurable]
findings.problem: The two proofs are line-for-line copies. Each one (a) rewrites to `MemLp 1`, (b) converts `essSup ‖g‖ₑ ≠ ∞` to `eLpNorm g ∞ μ ≠ ∞`, and (c) redoes a Hölder `calc` with `eLpNorm_smul_le_mul_eLpNorm_of_pos`, with p and q swapped. This is the same argument as `MemLp.smul` for exponents (∞,1,1) and (1,∞,1). The file already packages it as `Integrable.smul_of_top_right` and `Integrable.smul_of_top_left` (lines 981 and 991). So the Hölder step is proved three times in this file, and the essSup-to-`MemLp ∞` step is proved twice.
findings.proposed_change: Add a small lemma `memLp_top_of_essSup_enorm_ne_top (hg : AEStronglyMeasurable g μ) (h : essSup (‖g ·‖ₑ) μ ≠ ∞) : MemLp g ∞ μ := ⟨hg, by rw [eLpNorm_exponent_top hg]; exact h.lt_top⟩`. Then prove `Integrable.essSup_smul` as `hf.smul_of_top_right (memLp_top_of_essSup_enorm_ne_top g_aestronglyMeasurable ess_sup_g)` after rewriting the goal's `fun x => g x • f x` to `g • f`. Prove `Integrable.smul_essSup` as `hf.smul_of_top_left (memLp_top_of_essSup_enorm_ne_top …)`. This needs the two `smul_of_top_*` lemmas moved before line 571, or the two `smul_essSup`/`essSup_smul` lemmas moved after them. Because `MemLp.smul` only needs `MulActionWithZero`, `smul_of_top_left` can have `[Module 𝕜 β]` relaxed to `[MulActionWithZero 𝕜 β]` so `smul_essSup` keeps its current generality. Alternatively, keep the proofs where they are and call `MemLp.smul` directly, using the helper lemma only. The two `Quotient.lean` uses of `essSup_smul` are unaffected because the statement is unchanged.
findings.benefit: This removes two 7-line copies of the Hölder `calc` (with its `simpa using!` instance-unification step). Hölder for L^∞ × L^1 is then proved once, in `MemLp.smul`. The essSup conversion is stated once. A reader sees that both lemmas are the L^∞ × L^1 case of `smul_of_top_*`. Future generalisation (the file's TODO about enorm classes) needs to be done in one place.
